name: Terah (Abraham's father)
title: Patriarch from Ur of the Chaldeans
summary: Terah was the father of Abraham, Nahor, and Haran, and an ancestor of the Hebrew people. He led his family out of Ur of the Chaldeans with the aim of traveling to Canaan but settled in Haran where he died. According to Jewish tradition, he was an idol worshiper before Abraham received God's call.

keyEvents.title: Terah's lineage presented
keyEvents.description: The Bible gives a genealogical overview of Terah's family, including his three sons Abraham, Nahor, and Haran, who were born in Ur of the Chaldeans.

keyEvents.title: Haran's death in Ur
keyEvents.description: Terah's son Haran died in his birthplace Ur of the Chaldeans while his father was still alive. Haran was the father of Lot.

keyEvents.title: The Migration from Ur
keyEvents.description: Terah took Abraham, Lot and Sarai and left Ur of the Chaldeans to go to the land of Canaan, but they stopped in Haran and settled there.

keyEvents.title: Terah's Death in Haran
keyEvents.description: Terah lived 205 years and died in Haran. After his death, God called Abraham to continue the journey to Canaan.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Joshua's Speech
keyEvents.description: Joshua reminded the people that their ancestors, including Terah, had lived on the other side of the Euphrates and worshiped other gods.
